chapter: The rhythm section, family and records
title: The All-American Rhythm Section Decca session, about 1938
summary: Hinton introduces their rhythm section records; Jones recalls recording on two mikes at Decca with Basie, Green and Page.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Hey, Jo, I want to play this record here now. This is a recording of without a doubt the greatest rhythm section that was ever put together and it consists of this - it's called the All-American Rhythm Section and it still is and always was and without a doubt recognized by the entire world as the greatest rhythm section that was ever in the music business and the dance band, and that's Jo Jones, Count Basie, Freddie Green, and the very great late Walter Page. Do you want to tell me anything about this first one, how you guys did this?

We walked in the studio just to make, just to record the rhythm. The Mills Brothers was in another studio in Decca Recording and they came in and saw us doing this. At the time we were playing blue phrases. Basie was not familiar, which I was familiar with the blues and which I had to tell Walter Page, because Walter Page knew Joe Pullam and we got together and we did this thing, only on two mikes, at Decca Recording studio.
Do you remember what year that was, Jo, about?
